conclusion: The reviewed public official and scholarly sources document a two-level museum, elevator, cinema steps and alternate ramp, historic suspended platforms, and the building's position in the Santa Chiara complex. None provides a current orthographic visitor plan or independently encoded floor surface/void. No indoor model, room anchor, sourceSpace or verticalLink can be generated without invention.

sources.title: Museo delle Sinopie accessibility audit
sources.finding: Summer 2024 audit. Page 2 states the museum is arranged on two levels. Page 7 explicitly records no visitor maps and no tactile maps. Page 8 documents the upper level by elevator and a cinema reached by three steps or a 4.90 m by 0.80 m rear-corridor ramp at 10.3 percent. Page 10 places the bookshop at the cinema level. It supplies operational topology but no plan geometry.

sources.title: Pisa restaurata. Un profilo della tutela e del restauro monumentale nella citta del Novecento
sources.institution: Edizioni della Normale / Scuola Normale Superiore
sources.finding: Page-by-page text and visual audit found Sinopie references but no plan of the museum in the former Ospedale Nuovo di Santo Spirito. Plan-like pages concern other buildings or infrastructure.

sources.title: Pisa 292, Santa Chiara international design competition, elaborato 5
sources.finding: Pages 18 and 20 give competition-era site massing and the relationship of buildings 1, 2 and 9. Page 20 states that the complex contains the Sinopie Museum on the north side. These are context/proposal diagrams, not a current museum interior visitor plan.

onlineSourcesInvestigated.finding: Official census dates the project to 1971-1979, credits Gaetano Nencini and Giovanna Piancastelli Politi, and describes an internal parallelepiped volume with platforms at different heights. No public plan download was found.
Official page confirms the great rectangular Peregrinaio hall, the 1970s installation, and a 2005 visitor-information area. It provides no plan.

Indexed scholarly article describes horizontal and vertical use, a ticket-desk filter, the elevator column, and platforms at different heights; figures document the installation. The PDF endpoint repeatedly failed TLS transfer in this environment, and no indexed text identifies an orthographic plan. No geometry was taken from snippets.
A 2024 record approves in-person archival consultation of restoration documents. It confirms non-public archival material exists but does not expose a usable plan.
Catalog record for the 1979 museum publication; no digital plan or full text is attached.
Archive catalog records related museum material but does not publish an indoor plan in the reviewed public item.
